title: Radial Hyperbolic Measures: Shell Geometry, Pyramid Limits, and Gaussian Phase Transitions
summary: In high-dimensional hyperbolic space, concentration of a radial measure near a shell need not determine the pyramid limit: angular concentration and hyperbolic expansion alter separation. An effective radius is the scale on which positive-mass sets actually separate, which the raw radius need not give. With vanishing rescaling and radial fluctuations, radius convergence gives weak convergence to the pyramid of all metric measure spaces with the resulting diameter bound.
